page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 24 physical cores and 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 188.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 3.91 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a 960 GB SSD, and the instance operates under a QEMU hypervisor. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong CPU performance, with both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests placing in the top 25%. The AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong capabilities in specialized tasks, scoring in the top 25% for Passmark CPU physics, encryption, and extended instructions. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is also strong, though read-only memory bandwidth remains in the average tier. In database operations, the server performs strongly, achieving 64.55 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and ranking in the top 25% for Passmark database operations. For language model tasks, the server achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small 135M models, though performance drops to average for medium and large models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx63 offers a high density of dedicated compute resources and a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio of nearly 1:4, making it a viable option for resource-intensive workloads without the premium of specialized memory-optimized hardware. The presence of dedicated AMD EPYC cores makes this instance well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database hosting, and moderate-scale web serving.
